title: Settlement Economy: production, consumption and trade of goods
about: The implementation of design.json: where the work goes (repositories), components in dependency order, and per feature: the design elements it serves, the code it changes (anchors in the mod source), the data it adds, the features it comes after, its tasks (each todo or done), acceptance and checks. A feature is done when every task is done and every check passes. tools/check_plan.py validates design, plan and requests together.

mod.access: GitLab MCP tools (mcp__gitlab__*); no separate authorization needed
mod.rule: All Settlement Economy mod work goes to this test branch; main stays untouched until the user decides (R3)

files.what: The design statement, verbatim from the user (prompt M16)
The design structure: summary, the statement as elements (each quoting its text), and every decision with its source
The implementation: repositories and branch, invariants, components, features (design elements served, code anchors, data, order, tasks with status, acceptance, checks)
Every prompt of the work verbatim with what it led to, and the requests split into items with status and location
Proposed unit, category, land kind and need of every good
Generated by tools/catalogue.py: every resource from the mod XML, its origins, the building chains
Generated by tools/callsites.py: every call reading a plot resource token, classified
Written by tools/check_plan.py <checkout>: which features pass their checks, broken anchors, mod commit and branch
In-game confirmations of manual checks, by check id

components.title: Geography and tiles
components.player_sees: No resource tokens on the map. The land itself has qualities: crop and herd suitability, ore grade and depth, fishing grounds, shown in the plot help and a map overlay. What a tile yields follows its qualities and the improvement built on it; the improvement decides which of the plot's qualities it uses (a farm the crops, a pasture the herds, a mine the ore). Techs keep adding yield as they do now. A city still gains a resource as today, from an improved, connected tile, but the tile's quality is the source instead of a placed token. Forests yield timber through lumber camps (early) and lumbermills (Machinery). Pastures yield every good of their animals: cows meat, dairy and leather; sheep meat, wool, dairy and leather; horses horses and leather. Every good, the new ones included, has its own realistic icon.

resume: The files, not memory or a summary, hold the work. A new or compacted session starts here.
1. Save any new prompt verbatim in requests.json (prompts, and a request with items if it asks for something) before other work.
2. Read statement.md, then run tools/check_plan.py --summary: open requests, design coverage, decisions, progress, the features that can start and their open tasks.

3. Mod work goes only to the branch in plan.json repositories.mod, through the GitLab MCP tools. With a local checkout of that branch: tools/catalogue.py and tools/callsites.py, then tools/check_plan.py <checkout> to refresh status.json.
4. Work only on features the summary lists as able to start. Mark each finished task with tools/check_plan.py task <ID> done, and each finished request item with tools/check_plan.py item <ID> done.
5. New decisions go into design.json, changed features into plan.json, in the same commit as the work.
